title: The Three Wells Caravanserai
teaser: The camels are untouched and the goods intact, but the merchant Bahram lies by the well with a scrap of someone else's turban in his hand. The gates were locked from the inside for the night, and the caravan hasn't moved. The guards saw a shadow, and then another one.

habits.label: Henna on the palms
clues: The wooden windlass of the well has reddish palm prints on it, the kind fresh henna leaves. The culprit's palms are dyed with henna.
There are henna-coloured finger marks on the white silk in the merchant's room. The culprit has henna on their palms.

habits.label: Carnelian prayer beads
clues: A drilled red carnelian bead was found in the sand by the well. The culprit carries carnelian prayer beads.
From the tower the guard heard the steady click of little stones in the dark courtyard, like prayer beads being told. The culprit fingers carnelian prayer beads.

habits.label: Smells of saxaul smoke
clues: Bahram's robe reeks of bitter saxaul smoke, and the hearth in his room wasn't lit. The culprit's clothes smell of saxaul smoke.
A saddle blanket in the stables smells of saxaul smoke, though the guests burn dried dung in their hearths. The culprit's clothes smell of saxaul.

habits.label: Chews cardamom
clues: Green cardamom husks are scattered on the stone rim of the well. The culprit chews cardamom.
The merchant's room smells of cardamom, though Bahram never carried spices. The culprit chews cardamom pods.

habits.label: Sabre scar
habits.habit: A sabre scar on the forearm
clues: From the tower the guard saw a bare arm with a long white scar by the well in the torchlight. The culprit has a sabre scar on their forearm.
Bahram's notebook has a line: "The man with the sabre scar asked about the silk again." The culprit has a sabre scar on their forearm.

habits.label: Turquoise ring
habits.habit: A turquoise ring on the little finger
clues: There's a deep scratch on Bahram's neck with a crumb of blue turquoise in it. The culprit wears a turquoise ring.
The rim of the well has a round scratch from a ring and some blue stone dust. The culprit wears a turquoise ring.

habits.label: Blue turban
clues: The scrap of turban in Bahram's hand is dyed with indigo, and the dye still stains fingers. The culprit wears a blue turban.
The well's windlass has blue streaks from wet indigo-dyed cloth. The culprit wears an indigo turban.

habits.label: Kohl-lined eyes
clues: There's a greasy black smear of kohl on the edge of the well. The culprit lines their eyes with kohl.
A copper kohl pot with a still-damp stick hangs on a nail in the stables. The culprit lines their eyes with kohl.

habits.label: Covers tracks
habits.habit: Reads and confuses tracks in the sand
clues: The footprints by the well run backwards and then stop, a trick only desert people know. The culprit can read and confuse tracks.
The sand by the stables has been smoothed with the hem of a robe so evenly that the guards found not a single print. The culprit knows how to cover tracks in the sand.

habits.label: Plays backgammon
clues: An unfinished game lies on the backgammon board in the teahouse, the stake next to it untouched. The culprit plays backgammon for money.
There's an IOU tucked into Bahram's belt: "For backgammon, forty coins, to be paid by dawn." The culprit plays backgammon.

habits.label: Hunting falcon
clues: A speckled falcon feather and a torn leather jess lie by the well. The culprit keeps a hunting falcon.
There are fresh droppings of a bird of prey and a lump of raw meat on a perch in the stables. The culprit keeps a hunting falcon.

habits.label: Arabic calligraphy
clues: There's an unsigned note in the merchant's room, written in fine, even Arabic script. The culprit writes beautiful Arabic calligraphy.
A few words in skilled calligraphy are traced with a finger in the wet sand by the well. The culprit has mastered Arabic script.

habits.label: Sings epics
habits.habit: Sings old epic songs from memory
clues: After midnight the guards heard someone softly chanting an old epic song by the well. The culprit sings epics.
The teahouse keeper says that in the evening someone sang Bahram the tale of Layla and Majnun, at length and without a single slip. The culprit sings epic songs from memory.

habits.label: Studded belt
clues: A brass plaque torn from a belt, with a scrap of leather still on it, lies in the sand by the well. The culprit wears a belt with brass plaques.
From the tower the guard heard brass jingling in the dark courtyard, like plaques on a belt. The culprit wears a belt with brass plaques.

habits.label: Gold tooth
clues: By torchlight the tower guard saw a smile with a gleam of gold by the well. The culprit has a gold tooth.
A receipt in Bahram's possession describes the buyer: "gold tooth in front". The culprit has a gold tooth.

habits.label: Dagger in a sheath
habits.habit: A dagger in a silver sheath at the belt
clues: The stone rim of the well has a long scratch from the silver fittings of a sheath. The culprit carries a dagger in a silver sheath.
The silk of Bahram's robe has a shiny grey mark, as if a silver sheath had rubbed against it. The culprit carries a dagger in a silver sheath.

strong: Bahram was lifted and slung over the stone rim of the well. The culprit is physically strong.
A sack of barley weighing over thirty kilos was dragged from the storehouse and propped against the stable door. The culprit is physically strong.
passages: The gates are locked from the inside, but the dung hatch in the back wall of the stables is open. The culprit knows the service passages.
An old dry irrigation ditch runs from the watchtower to the storehouse, and there are wet footprints on its steps. The culprit knows the service passages.
keys: The heavy lock on the storehouse was opened and locked again without a single scratch. The culprit had keys.
The postern by the watchtower was unlocked from the inside with its own key. The culprit had keys.
cash: The gold coins are gone from Bahram's purse, but the copper was left. The culprit had access to money.
In the owner's account book, the sum for Bahram's lodging has been altered, and the ink is fresh. The culprit had access to money.
tools: The chain of the well's windlass was unriveted and put back together. The culprit is handy with tools.
The bar on the gates was lifted off its brackets, and the nails were later driven back into the same holes. The culprit is handy with tools.
french: There's a note in the merchant's room: "La soie est à moi". The culprit knows French.
A letter from the Lyon weavers in Bahram's bag has been opened, with notes in French in the margins. The culprit knows French.
quiet: The camels by the well sleep lightly, yet not one of them raised its head. The culprit moves silently.
The well is ringed with gravel where every step can be heard, yet the guards heard nothing. The culprit moves silently.
medic: There are no wounds on Bahram's body, but his lips have turned blue. The culprit knows about poisons.
The tea bowl Bahram took with him to the well has a bitter residue. The culprit knows about poisons.
safe: The money changer's iron-bound chest with a puzzle lock was opened without a single scratch. The culprit knows the safe combination.
Bahram's iron casket with a combination lock is open, and the promissory notes are gone. The culprit knows the safe combination.
perfume: A thick, sweet smell of rose oil hangs by the well. The culprit wears heavy perfume.
The scrap of turban in Bahram's hand is soaked in heavy musk. The culprit wears heavy perfume.
cane: There are round holes in the sand by the well from a staff with an iron tip. The culprit walks with a cane.
The guard heard a stick tapping on the courtyard stones all the way to the well. The culprit walks with a cane.
glasses: A thin round lens from a pair of glasses lies in the sand by the well. The culprit wears glasses.
There's an empty glasses case on the table in the merchant's room, and Bahram didn't wear glasses. The culprit wears glasses.
whistle: The guards on the tower heard someone in the courtyard whistling a caravan tune. The culprit whistles.
The camels in the stables raised their heads at quiet whistling behind the wall. The culprit likes to whistle.
